On a controlled null with the true nonlinearity fixed, raw 1-sim falls 48% as D/N sweeps 0.032 -> 0.500 (0.096803 -> 0.049933), which spans this zoo (gpt2 ships at _meta_d_over_n_tokens = 0.059558; the widest models sit near 0.42). procrustes_nonlinearity_corrected_mean removes that to within 0.15% on the isotropic null and 0.6% on the deterministic-nonlinearity null, and gpt2 now emits 0.020317 / 0.094527. ModelOutputCache still does not initialise self._last_block_raw or self._embedding_states in __init__ -- both are created only at the end of _run_forward_pass and reset in clear(). get_hidden_states is safe today because it returns early on `self._hidden_states is None` and the three are assigned together, but any future path that populates _hidden_states directly raises AttributeError. Two lines in __init__.

include_embedding has no shape guard, unlike replace_final_norm which checks tuple(self._last_block_raw.shape) == tuple(_hs[_lastk].shape). A desynchronised _embedding_states would be prepended silently; the pair would then fail _procrustes_similarity's shape check and become NaN rather than raising.
The dimension correction uses D/N where the exact null for a column-centered cloud is D/(N-1). Worth 5e-6 relative at N = 12895 -- cosmetic, but the anchor should be exact.

procrustes_nonlinearity_corrected_* is guarded only by 0 < D/N < 1, so at small num_samples the divisor becomes tiny and the correction amplifies noise (25x at D/N = 0.96) with no warning or _meta_ flag.

_meta_n_tokens is still whatever the tokenizer produces from 100 documents (12895 on gpt2, 12895-14506 across the zoo), so tokenizer compression leaks into the raw score even though the corrected twin absorbs most of it.

BLME's pair set is now a superset of the reference's rather than equal to it (12 pairs vs 11: it adds block10->block11 at 0.931330). The docstring explains this, and the mean differs by only 0.46% (0.980893 vs 0.985399), but anyone comparing to the paper's per-layer figures should know the sets differ.
